name: Minriq
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Kruspe, Nicole, Niclas Burenhult & Ewelina Wnuk. 2015. Northern Aslian. In Jenny & Sidwell (eds.), The Handbook of Austroasiatic Languages. Brill. Covers Menriq/Minriq phonology; not freely online.

new_statements.quote: Stress falls invariably on the final syllable of words. Despite suggestions that some Northern Aslian varieties display marginal tonal contrasts (Hajek 2003), we have so far found no evidence of suprasegmental contrastive strategies in Jedek, neither tone nor register. [Dunn, Burenhult, Kruspe, Tufvesson & Becker 2011: 300, Aslian-wide, sample incl. Menriq Lah and Menriq Rual:] the final syllable in most Aslian languages always has the structure /CVC/. ... Also, the final syllable is the most informative part of a word in that it always receives stress and contains the greatest phonemic variation (Diffloth 1976: 102, p.c.).
new_statements.citation: Yager, Joanne & Niclas Burenhult. 2017. Jedek: a newly discovered Aslian variety of Malaysia. Linguistic Typology 21(3): 493-545. doi:10.1515/lingty-2017-0012.
new_statements.locator: p. 508, section 3.1.4 'Prosodic features' (statement is about Jedek, ex-'Menriq Rual', not Menriq of Kuala Lah); supporting family-wide statement Dunn et al. 2011: 300 (file../kint1239/)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK. lines 732-737 (page header '508 Joanne Yager and Niclas Burenhult' immediately above): '3.1.4 Prosodic features / Stress falls invariably on the final syllable of words. Also, the final syllable is the most informative part of a word in that it always receives stress and cont…
new_statements.rule_in_words: By the closest available evidence (Jedek, the sister variety formerly classed as 'Menriq Rual', and the Aslian-wide generalisation by the Lund team who hold the Menriq field data), word stress is fixed and non-contrastive on the final syllable of the word; no Menriq-specific published statement was found.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said for Jedek or Menriq (for the related Maniq, Wnuk & Burenhult 2014 report no secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: None for Jedek. Jedek clitics are unstressed (pp. 520-522). Skeat & Blagden 1906: 773 (generic 'Semang') claim occasional penultimate or even accent, an old impressionistic note.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement ('final syllable of words'); no discussion of phrase-level prominence or citation forms. Applies to a neighbouring variety, so for minr1238 this is inference from the subgroup, i.e. second-hand.
new_statements.identity_note: No published description of Menriq (minr1238, Kuala Lah, Gua Musang) phonology could be opened. The quoted stress sentence is for Jedek (Glottolog jede1239? -- the Sungai Rual variety formerly labelled 'Menriq Rual', Yager & Burenhult 2017), Menriq's closest relative within the Jahai-Menriq-Batek cluster; the supporting statement (Dunn et al. 2011: 300) is Aslian-wide. Malaysian work on 'bahasa Mendriq' (Fazal Mohamed Mohamed Sultan and UKM colleagues, Kg. Kuala Lah) is the same language as Glottolog Minriq but is syntax-only in what is accessible.

sources.locator: p. 508, section 3.1.4 'Prosodic features' (statement is about Jedek, ex-'Menriq Rual', not Menriq of Kuala Lah); supporting family-wide statement Dunn et al. 2011: 300 (file../kint1239/)
sources.note: p. 508 sec. 3.1.4: 'Stress falls invariably on the final syllable of words' -- but this describes JEDEK (Sungai Rual; the variety formerly labelled 'Menriq Rual'), Menriq's closest relative, not Menriq of Kuala Lah. Menriq appears only as a comparandum (e.g. p. 507: closed final syllables in Jahai, Batek, Menriq); no Menriq stress statement.

sources.citation: Benjamin, Geoffrey. 2012. The Aslian languages of Malaysia and Thailand: an assessment. Language Documentation and Description 11: 136-230.
sources.note: Survey. p. 179: Aslian 'major (i.e., stressed, word-final) vowel systems'; p. 187 sec. 4.2.4 quotes Dunn et al. 2011 on final-syllable stress. Mentions Menriq only for Carey 1970 wordlist and Fazal et al. syntax; no Menriq-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Dunn, Michael, Niclas Burenhult, Nicole Kruspe, Sylvia Tufvesson & Neele Becker. 2011. Aslian linguistic prehistory: a case study in computational phylogenetics. Diachronica 28(3): 291-323 (author postprint, MPG PuRe).
sources.note: p. 300, family-wide: 'the final syllable is the most informative part of a word in that it always receives stress' (citing Diffloth 1976: 102, p.c.); the sample includes Menriq Lah (Burenhult 2006, 2008, Kuala Lah) and Menriq Rual. Not a Menriq-specific description.

sources.note: p. 285 reports Schebesta (1928, BSOS 4) for Jahai: 'the accent falls on the last syllable of a word'. Discusses the Menri/Menrik of Kelantan ethnographically only.

sources.citation: Skeat, Walter W. & Charles O. Blagden. 1906. Pagan Races of the Malay Peninsula, vol. 2. London: Macmillan (archive.org djvu text).
sources.note: p. 773 'Accent': 'As a rule, the accent in all the aboriginal dialects appears to fall on the final syllable... the accent in Semang is usually on the final syllable, yet in some other dissyllables and polysyllables Semang accents the penultimate'. Generic 'Semang' (Northern Aslian), not Menriq-specific.
